title: Release Ops Circuit: intent-to-policy compiler for canary rollouts and auto-rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: Product teams need a reliable, auditable way to express high-level rollout intent (e.g., "make model B the default for 5% of traffic over 3 steps, abort if p95 latency or error_rate regresses > 3%") and have the platform compile that into concrete step schedules, traffic-split matrices, cohort selectors, plus automated rollback/mitigation actions. This ticket implements an "intent-to-policy" compiler (Release Ops Circuit) that: 1) accepts a compact DSL or JSON intent, 2) produces an executable rollout manifest (step timelines, traffic weights, shadow probes), 3) wires guardrails that evaluate multi-dimensional contracts (latency, errors, custom QA scores) and 4) triggers deterministic mitigation (rollback, throttle, re-route) with confidence scoring. Key design choices: - DSL + UI hybrid: users can author concise DSL but Console will render and allow edits. - Cohort-aware splits: enable percent by cohort (region, client tier) and shadow probing for specific slices. - Guardrail evaluation: sliding windows (1m, 5m, 1h) with configurable aggregation functions (median, p95) and statistical tests (bootstrap, Bayesian posterior). - Auto-rollback heuristic: multi-metric conjunctive rules with a Bayesian rollback confidence classifier that reduces noisy false positives. - Safety nets: canary quarantine (traffic escrow), shadow-only probes for riskier models, manual override with audit log. Implementation plan: Phase A (spec + compiler POC), Phase B (runtime checks + telemetry hooks), Phase C (Console UX + canary simulator), Phase D (customer trials + GA). Acceptance criteria: - Compiler converts intent examples in spec into rollout manifests and round-trips via Console. - Guardrail rules detect synthetic anomalies in integration test harness and trigger rollback automation. - End-to-end integration tests with Dedicated and Hosted modes demonstrating no user-facing regressions when shadow probes run. Data & telemetry: new event types 'ro_manifest.apply', 'ro_guardrail.violation', 'ro_action.rollback', 'ro_shadow.hit' with trace ids. Migration & compatibility: support existing rollout APIs by backwards-compatible translator. Security: rollout manifests are signed and require RBAC to execute. Risks & trade-offs: DSL expressivity vs complexity of guarantees (we limit advanced statistical ops initially), extra telemetry volume (mitigated by sampling), possible over-triggering of rollbacks (handled by confidence model).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Scoping kickoff: aligned with PM and Console on primary use cases (canary step schedules, cohort splits, shadow probes). Agreed to target a DSL that covers 90% of cases.

2026-03-03 - Architecture review: proposed compiler pipeline (parse -> expand cohorts -> schedule optimizer -> guardrail emitter) reviewed by Infra. Feedback: make guardrail evaluation pluggable and run in a separate, isolated worker pool.

2026-03-05 - Prototype: delivered POC that converts three canonical intents into rollout manifests and simulates traffic in the local harness. POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428
2026-03-07 - Perf note: early simulation indicates guardrail evaluator adds ~8ms median overhead per manifest evaluation; plan to batch evaluations and cache recent computations.
2026-03-08 - Telemetry dependency: blocked pending ENG-672041 (telemetry event schema extension) to add 'ro_guardrail.violation' fields. Reaching out to telemetry owners.

2026-03-10 - Design feedback from Security: require manifest signing and audit trail for any automatic rollback action; marked security_review_required. Next: implement signing and add KMS integration task.
Next steps: finish compiler unit tests, implement guardrail confidence classifier (Bayesian), wire up event emission and Console preview, then schedule integration run with Dedicated capacity team.
